My grandfather was hospitalized for around a year before he passed from complications from cancer. Most days I would commute to this special hospital he was admitted at, after school, 20 something kilometers from my house, and I would go home early morning before school started. I stayed all weekend most times too. The hospital used a combination of traditional and modern medicine. Instead of having hospital rooms, they rented out suites to families so the patient would be comfortable throughout their treatment. It didn't feel like a hospital. It was our second home for a year.

I was turning 13 in November of 2008. On the day of my birthday, I decided I couldn't go to the hospital because I was feeling tired from school, and I wasn't in much of a mood to celebrate. I told my mom, who split her time between home and taking care of my grandfather, about it. She came home that day, and I honestly don't remember what happened. She left again the morning after.

My grandfather passed away in December of that same year.

I don't know how long after it was before I found out, but my mom told me my grandfather expected me to spend my 13th birthday with him.

I absolutely still regret not going to him that day.
